Definition: Integration of CRVS data (births, deaths, marriages) into data exchange for real-time verification and service eligibility
Comments: EU-funded CRVS reform programme (CIVIPOL/Enabel) ran July 2020 to December 2023, aiming to create a centralised CRVS register linked to biometric database and interconnected with civil registration centres. Senegal is reported (November 2025) to be embedding CRVS within the national digital identity framework. Integration under development but not fully complete.
revision_notes: Original score (3, 2023) relied on the 2020-2023 CIVIPOL/Enabel programme description and a vague November 2025 trend piece, both superseded by more specific, more recent evidence. Fetched sources confirmed: (1) ANEC and DAF (the identity/civil-status file authority) signed an interoperability protocol in July 2025, with the national civil registration register (RNEC) now operational and 20m records digitised; (2) a national interministerial data-exchange platform (Jokkoo/X-Road, JICA-supported) launched April 2025, pilot 2024-25, full rollout 2025-27; (3) ANEC signed an interoperability protocol with the national statistics agency (ANSD) in January 2026 for automated exchange of civil-status data; (4) as of the June 2026 NEKKAL programme close-out, 400 civil registration centres are interconnected via a shared platform and a birth/death notification tool linking health facilities to civil registration has been built, though the EU and government note governance, reliability and archival gaps remain unresolved. This is evidence of real, multi-sector (ID, statistics, health) integration rather than mere development, so the score is raised from 3 (Under development) to 4 (Partially integrated). Not full integration since coverage/reliability gaps are explicitly acknowledged.
revised_comments: Senegal's civil registration and vital statistics (CRVS) data is now partially integrated into the government's data exchange architecture. Under the NEKKAL modernisation programme, over 20 million civil registration records have been digitised and some 400 civil registration centres are interconnected via the national civil registration register (RNEC), which became operational in 2025. The National Civil Registration Agency (ANEC) has signed interoperability protocols with the identity/civil-status file authority (DAF), enabling unique legal identity verification, and with the national statistics agency (ANSD, January 2026) for automated exchange of birth, marriage and death data supporting demographic planning. A notification tool linking health facilities to civil registration for real-time birth and death reporting has also been developed. These CRVS data flows sit within Senegal's broader interministerial data-exchange platform (Jokkoo, built on X-Road), launched in April 2025 and being rolled out in phases through 2027. Full integration is not yet complete: government and EU partners acknowledge continuing challenges around governance, data reliability, service accessibility and archive conservation.

revision_notes: Confirmed via DLA Piper (updated 2026) that Act No. 2008-12 of 25 January 2008 on Personal Data Protection remains the governing legislation, with the CDP (Commission des Données Personnelles) as oversight authority. A March 2026 APS interview with a cybersecurity/privacy expert and a Lequotidien report on a CDP-led workshop confirm the 2008 law is still in force but is widely regarded as outdated for AI/Big Data-era data governance; a revised bill (updating the 2019 draft) has been finalised by the CDP and is awaiting a vote in the National Assembly as of March 2026, alongside new National Data and AI strategies. Because primary enabling legislation for data processing and sharing by the state already exists and remains in force, the original score of 3 (Yes) is confirmed rather than changed; only the evidentiary basis and year are refreshed. No evidence found of a separate law specifically governing the data-exchange/interoperability platform itself (Jokkoo), which operates instead under executive/ministerial arrangements (New Deal Technologique, SENUM SA).
revised_comments: Senegal's data exchange system operates under an established legal framework. Act No. 2008-12 of 25 January 2008 on the Protection of Personal Data (with its 2008 implementing decree) provides the legal basis for the collection, processing, transfer and sharing of personal data by the state, local authorities and other bodies, and created the Commission des Données Personnelles (CDP) as the independent oversight authority. Senegal ratified the African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection in 2016. This 2008 law remains in force and continues to underpin cross-government data sharing, although it is widely viewed by legal and cybersecurity experts as outdated for addressing artificial intelligence and big-data-era data governance. A revised Personal Data Protection Bill, developed with the CDP and updated to align with the government's National Data Strategy and National AI Strategy, is finalised and pending a vote in the National Assembly.
